physicalNotes: Radius 0.0981356 Jupiter radii from Adams et al. 2021 (2021PSJ.....2..152A), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2021PSJ.....2..152A/abstract): 7,015.9 km at 71,492 km per Jupiter radius. GM from the mass 0.0043 Jupiter masses (the NASA Exoplanet Archive's calculated value (M-R relationship, its Chen & Kipping 2017 mass-radius relationship): a model, not a measurement, via the NASA Exoplanet Archive, https://exoplanetarchive.ipac.caltech.edu/docs/pscp_calc.html) times JPL's Jupiter GM. A sphere: no oblateness is measured.

sources.period: Mayo et al. 2018 (2018AJ....155..136M), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname MAYO_ET_AL__2018): P 0.813149 d
sources.shape: Adams et al. 2021 (2021PSJ.....2..152A), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname ADAMS_ET_AL__2021): a/R* 4.4; Adams et al. 2021 (2021PSJ.....2..152A), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname ADAMS_ET_AL__2021): inclination 89.8 degrees
sources.eccentricity: No archive row states an eccentricity; the orbit is taken as circular
sources.phase: Mayo et al. 2018 (2018AJ....155..136M), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname MAYO_ET_AL__2018): transit mid-time 2457583.14093 BJD, taken as BJD_TDB; with its period, the row that predicts 2026-01-01 best (1 sigma 306 min)
sources.orientation: Display convention: transit photometry does not measure the orbit's position angle on the sky, so the ascending node is set at position angle 0 (celestial north).
